Use this action when you need to: - Automatically assign tickets based on conditions - Change ticket priority/status based on rules - Add tags to tickets matching certain criteria - Notify agents or teams based on ticket properties - Implement escalation workflows Note: Automations must have at least one condition that is time-based (like created_at, updated_at) OR check one of: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, or requester_id.

At least one 'all' condition must reference a time-based field (created_at, updated_at, etc.) or check: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, or requester_id. Omitting it would post `{"all": [], "any": []}` to Zendesk and fail server-side.

Use conditions to specify which records to delete - for time-based ticket deletion, use 'duration_since_last_update'; for time-based end-user ('zen:user') deletion, use 'duration_since_last_activity' instead — both with a 'greater_than' operator and ISO 8601 duration values (e.g., 'P30D' for 30 days).

group_id.description: The numeric ID of the group to assign the agent to. You can find this from group list results or ticket group_id fields.

group_memberships.create.title: Create Zendesk Group Membership

tickets.import_many.description: Bulk import tickets into Zendesk by posting up to 100 ticket objects at a time. Use when migrating tickets from another system or creating multiple tickets in a single API call. The operation returns a job_status payload; the initial status is typically 'queued' or 'completed' for small batches. This action is useful for data migration, test data setup, and bulk ticket creation workflows.

tickets.description: Array of up to 100 ticket objects to import. Each ticket can have any valid ticket field.

archive_immediately.description: If true, any ticket created with a 'closed' status bypasses the normal ticket lifecycle and will be created directly in your ticket archive

tickets.import_many.title: Bulk Import Tickets

dynamic_content.variants.create_many.description: Create many locale variants for an existing dynamic content item in Zendesk. Use when you need to add multiple language variants to a dynamic content item in a single operation. This action is efficient for bulk-adding translations to support multilingual content. This action is idempotent - running it multiple times with the same variants will create duplicate variants if they don't already exist. Consider listing existing variants first to avoid duplicates.

variants.description: Array of locale variants to create. Each variant provides content for a specific locale.

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The ID of the dynamic content item to add variants to.

dynamic_content.variants.create_many.title: Create Many Dynamic Content Variants

tickets.create_many.description: Create many tickets in Zendesk in a single request. Accepts an array of up to 100 ticket objects. The operation is handled asynchronously — a background job is queued and you receive a job_status payload with an initial status of 'queued' or 'working'. Poll the job_status URL or use ZENDESK_GET_APPS_JOB_STATUS to check for completion and view per-ticket results. Use when creating multiple tickets at once or seeding test data. This action is irreversible — tickets created cannot be easily undone once the job completes. Ensure the tickets list is accurate before submitting.

tickets.description: Array of ticket objects to create (max 100). Each ticket requires at minimum a 'subject' field.

tickets.create_many.title: Create Many Zendesk Tickets

users.create_many.description: Create many users in Zendesk in a single request. Accepts up to 100 user objects. The operation is handled asynchronously — a background job is queued and you receive a job_status payload with an initial status of 'queued' or 'working'. Poll the job_status URL or use ZENDESK_GET_APPS_JOB_STATUS to check for completion and view per-user results. Use when onboarding multiple users at once or seeding test data. Note: This action is idempotent — re-running with the same external_ids may update existing users depending on Zendesk configuration.

users.description: Array of user objects to create (max 100). Each user requires a 'name' field.

skip_verify_email.description: If true, do not send verification emails to new users. Passed as a URL query parameter.

users.create_many.title: Create Many Zendesk Users

object_triggers.create.description: Create a new trigger for a custom object in Zendesk. Custom object triggers are business rules that automatically perform actions when certain conditions are met on custom object records. Use this action when you need to: - Send notifications when custom object records are created or updated - Automatically update fields on custom object records - Add or remove tags based on custom object conditions - Implement automated workflows for custom object data This action is idempotent - creating a trigger with the same name multiple times will result in duplicate triggers unless the name is changed.

title.description: The title/name of the trigger. Must be unique within the custom object.

active.description: Whether the trigger is active and will execute. Set to false to create a draft trigger.

actions.description: List of actions the trigger will perform when conditions are met. Each action specifies a field and value.

position.description: The position of the trigger which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

conditions.description: The conditions that must be met for the trigger to execute. Conditions use 'all' (AND) and 'any' (OR) logic.

description.description: A description of what the trigger does.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object to create a trigger for. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

object_triggers.create.title: Create Object Trigger

organization_fields.create.description: Create a custom organization field in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new custom field type (such as text, dropdown, checkbox, date, etc.) to track additional organization attributes. The field key must be unique and can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores.

key.description: A unique key that identifies this custom field. Must consist of only letters, numbers, and underscores. Cannot be only numbers.

tag.description: Optional tag for checkbox type fields

title.description: The title of the custom field

active.description: If true, this field is available for use. Defaults to true.

position.description: Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Lower values appear first.

description.description: User-defined description of the field's purpose

relationship_filter.description: Filter definition for autocomplete in lookup fields

custom_field_options.description: Required for dropdown or multiselect types. Each option requires a name and value.

regexp_for_validation.description: Regular expression pattern for validating regexp type fields

organization_fields.create.title: Create Organization Field

organization_memberships.create.description: Create a new organization membership in Zendesk by assigning a user to an organization. Use when you need to associate a user with an organization so they can access organization-specific tickets and data. Returns a 422 error if the user is already assigned to the organization. This action is idempotent in that creating a duplicate membership will fail with a specific error, but the operation itself is not naturally idempotent.

default.description: Denotes whether this is the default organization membership for the user. If set to true, this membership will be the primary organization for the user. Defaults to true if not specified.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to assign to the organization. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to assign the user to. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION_BY_ID; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

organization_memberships.create.title: Create Organization Membership

organization_memberships.create_many.description: Create multiple organization memberships in Zendesk by posting up to 100 membership objects at a time. Each membership links a user to an organization. Use when onboarding multiple users to organizations in bulk, such as during team migrations or organizational restructuring. The operation returns a job_status payload; the initial status is typically 'queued' for larger batches.

organization_memberships.description: Array of organization membership objects to create (max 100). Each object requires user_id and organization_id.

organization_memberships.create_many.title: Create Many Organization Memberships

organizations.merge.description: Merge two Zendesk organizations by combining all users, tickets, and data from the losing organization into the winning organization. This action is irreversible — once merged, the losing organization and all its data cannot be recovered. Use when you need to consolidate duplicate organizations or combine organization data into a single organization.

winner_id.description: The ID of the winning organization that will receive all users and tickets from the losing organization

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to merge from (the losing organization that will be merged into another)

organizations.merge.title: Merge Zendesk Organizations

organizations.tags.create.description: Set organization tags in Zendesk by making a POST request to replace the tags on an organization. Use when you need to categorize or label organizations with specific tags for filtering and organization purposes. This operation replaces all existing tags on the organization with the new set provided. Note: This action is not idempotent as it replaces existing tags rather than adding to them.

tags.description: An array of tag strings to set for the organization. Tags are used to categorize and filter organizations. Existing tags on the organization will be replaced with this new set of tags.

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to set tags for. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

organizations.tags.create.title: Set Organization Tags

organization_subscriptions.create.description: Create an organization subscription in Zendesk. This subscribes a user to receive notifications and updates related to a specific organization. Use when you need to add a user to an organization's subscription list so they can access organization-related resources and receive notifications.

user_id.description: The ID of the user who will be subscribed to the organization

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to subscribe the user to

organization_subscriptions.create.title: Create Organization Subscription

users.create_or_update_many.description: Create or update multiple users in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to batch create or update up to 100 users at once. New users require a 'name' field; existing users are matched by 'id'. Returns a job_status with results for each operation. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same results.

users.description: Array of user objects to create or update. Up to 100 users can be included. For new users, 'name' is required. For existing users, 'id' is required to identify the user to update.

users.create_or_update_many.title: Create Or Update Many Users

organizations.create_or_update.description: Create or update a Zendesk organization in a single operation. If an organization with the same external_id already exists, it is updated. Otherwise, a new organization is created. Use when you need to ensure an organization exists without checking for duplicates first. Note: For updates, you must specify the external_id to match the existing organization. Name is not available as a matching criteria.

name.description: A unique name for the organization. Required when creating a new organization. Note: Name is not available as a matching criteria for updates - use external_id or id instead.

notes.description: Any notes you have about the organization

details.description: Any details about the organization, such as the address

group_id.description: New tickets from users in this organization are automatically put in this group

external_id.description: A unique external id to associate organizations to an external record. The id is case-insensitive (e.g., 'company1' and 'Company1' are considered the same). Use this for matching when updating an existing organization.

domain_names.description: An array of domain names associated with this organization

shared_tickets.description: End users in this organization are able to see each other's tickets

shared_comments.description: End users in this organization are able to comment on each other's tickets

organization_fields.description: Custom fields for this organization. See custom organization fields documentation for available field definitions.

organizations.create_or_update.title: Create Or Update Organization

users.create_or_update.description: Create or update a Zendesk user. If a user with the same email or external_id exists, it updates that user. Otherwise, it creates a new user. Use when you need to upsert user records - idempotent based on email or external_id matching. Returns 200 for existing users, 201 for newly created users.

user.description: User object with attributes. `name` is mandatory. The user is matched by `email` or `external_id` to determine create vs update. `role` must be one of: 'end-user', 'agent', or 'admin'.

users.create_or_update.title: Create or Update User

push_notification_devices.destroy_many.description: Bulk unregister push notification devices in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the devices will be permanently removed from receiving push notifications and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete device tokens or removing test devices from receiving push notifications.

push_notification_devices.description: List of mobile device tokens to unregister from push notifications. These are the device tokens returned when a mobile device registers for push notifications.

push_notification_devices.destroy_many.title: Bulk Unregister Push Notification Devices

resource_collections.create.description: Create a resource collection in Zendesk. Use when you need to batch multiple operations on Zendesk resources (like tickets) into a single request. The API processes the collection as a background job and returns a job status object. Note: This action queues a background job. Poll the returned job_status.url to check when the collection has been processed.

title.description: The title/name of the resource collection. This is used to identify the collection.

actions.description: Array of action objects specifying what to do with the resources. Each action has a type and list of resource IDs.

resource_collections.create.title: Create Resource Collection

side_conversations.create.description: Create a private side conversation on a Zendesk ticket. Side conversations are agent-to-agent communications that don't notify the customer. Use this action when you need to discuss a ticket privately with another agent, escalate to a specialist, or coordinate on sensitive issues without customer visibility. Recipients can include Zendesk users (by ID or email), Slack channels, support groups, or Microsoft Teams channels.

to.description: List of recipients for the side conversation. Each recipient must have at least one of: user_id, email, slack_channel_id, support_group_id, or msteams_channel_id. At least one recipient is required.

body.description: Plain text body of the initial message. This is the main content of the side conversation that recipients will see.

subject.description: Subject line for the side conversation. If not provided, a default subject may be used based on the parent ticket.

html_body.description: HTML-formatted body of the initial message. If provided, this will be used instead of the plain text body for HTML-capable clients.

ticket_id.description: The ID of the Zendesk ticket to attach the side conversation to

external_ids.description: Key-value external metadata to attach to the side conversation. Use this to store custom identifiers or tags from your external systems.

attachment_ids.description: List of attachment file IDs to include with the message. These must be IDs from previously uploaded attachments via the CreateSideConversationAttachment action.

side_conversations.create.title: Create Side Conversation

recipient_addresses.create.description: Create a new support address (recipient address) in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new email address for receiving support requests. The email address must follow Zendesk's format (`{local-part}@{accountname}.zendesk.com`) for internal addresses, or be an existing external email with forwarding properly configured. The created address will have verification statuses that indicate whether DNS records (CNAME, SPF) are properly configured. Note that you cannot change the email address of an existing support address after creation.

name.description: The name for the address

address_email.description: The email address for the support address. Note: You cannot change the email address of an existing support address after creation.

default.description: Whether this address should be the account's default support address

brand_id.description: The ID of the brand to associate with this support address. If not provided, the address will be associated with the account's default brand.

recipient_addresses.create.title: Create Support Address

suspended_tickets.export.description: Export Suspended Tickets from Zendesk Support. Use when you need to export all suspended tickets for compliance review, audit purposes, or data analysis. This action enqueues a job that creates a CSV file; when complete, Zendesk emails the requester a link to download the CSV. Suspended tickets are sorted by update timestamp in ascending order. Rate limited to one request per minute. Note: This action is read-only and returns the export job status. The actual CSV will be sent via email when the job completes.
suspended_tickets.export.title: Export Suspended Tickets

tickets.content_pins.create.description: Create a ticket content pin in Zendesk. Content pins allow you to attach helpful resources like Help Center articles or external content directly to tickets for easy reference. Use this action when you need to: - Attach a Help Center article to a ticket for context - Pin an external knowledge base article to a ticket - Add relevant documentation or resources to a support ticket

locale.description: The locale for the content pin. Required when content_type is 'external_content' — Zendesk rejects external-content pins with no locale ('External contents must have locale to be able to get pinned to tickets.'). Also required when pinning articles. Format: language + underscore + locale code (e.g., 'en-us', 'fr-ca').

ticket_id.description: The ID of the ticket to which the content pin will be added

content_id.description: The ID of the content to pin

content_type.description: The type of content being pinned. Common values include 'article' for Help Center articles and 'external_content' for external resources.

tickets.content_pins.create.title: Create Ticket Content Pin

ticket_fields.create.description: Create a custom ticket field in Zendesk with various field types. Use when you need to add a new custom field (such as text, dropdown, checkbox, date, numeric, regex-validated, or lookup) to capture additional information on tickets. The field title is required; description, required flag, and custom options are optional.

tag.description: For checkbox fields only. The tag added to tickets when the checkbox is selected

title.description: The title of the ticket field shown to agents and end users

active.description: If true, this field is available for use. Defaults to true.

position.description: Relative position of the field on the ticket. Fields with lower positions appear first.

required.description: If true, agents must enter a value in this field to change the ticket status to solved. Defaults to false.

description.description: User-defined description explaining the purpose of this field

agent_can_edit.description: If true, agents can edit this field. Defaults to true.

title_in_portal.description: The title shown to end users in Help Center (may differ from agent title)

agent_description.description: A description of the ticket field that only agents can see

visible_in_portal.description: If true, the field is visible to end users in Help Center. Defaults to true.

editable_in_portal.description: If true, end users can edit this field in Help Center. Defaults to true.

required_in_portal.description: If true, end users must enter a value to create a request. Defaults to false.

relationship_filter.description: Filter definition that allows autocomplete to filter down results for lookup fields

collapsed_for_agents.description: If true, the field is hidden alongside infrequently used fields. Classic interface only.

custom_field_options.description: Required for multiselect and tagger types. Defines the available options for dropdown selection.

regexp_for_validation.description: Regular expression pattern for validating input on regexp type fields

ticket_fields.create.title: Create Ticket Field

ticket_fields.options.create.description: Create or update an option for a dropdown or multiselect ticket field. Use when you need to add a new selectable option to a custom ticket field of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'. If an option with the same value already exists, it will be updated with the provided name. This action is idempotent - running it multiple times with the same value will update the existing option rather than creating duplicates.

name.description: The name of the option displayed to agents and end users in the dropdown

value.description: The internal value of the option used when saving the ticket field selection

position.description: The relative position of the option in the dropdown list. Options with lower positions appear first.

allow_solving.description: If true, selecting this option allows the ticket to be solved when the field is required to solve

ticket_field_id.description: The ID of the ticket field to add the option to. The ticket field must be of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'.

ticket_fields.options.create.title: Create Ticket Field Option

triggers.create.description: Create a new trigger in Zendesk. Triggers are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Unlike automations, triggers execute immediately when tickets are created or updated. Use this action when you need to: - Automatically change ticket status based on conditions - Assign tickets to agents or groups based on rules - Add tags to tickets matching certain criteria - Send notifications to agents, groups, or external systems - Update custom fields based on ticket properties Note: Triggers must have at least one condition in the 'all' array that references a time-based field (like created_at, updated_at) OR checks one of: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, requester_id, custom_status_id.

title.description: The title/name of the trigger. Must be unique among all triggers.

active.description: Whether the trigger is active and will execute. Set to false to create a draft trigger.

actions.description: List of actions the trigger will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

conditions.description: The conditions that must be met for the trigger to execute. At least one 'all' condition must reference a time-based field (created_at, updated_at) or check: status, type, group_id, assignee_id, requester_id, custom_status_id.

category_id.description: The ID of the category to assign the trigger to. Categories help organize triggers in the Zendesk admin interface.

description.description: A description of what the trigger does.

triggers.create.title: Create Trigger

trigger_categories.jobs.create.description: Create a batch job for ticket trigger categories in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to perform batch operations on multiple trigger categories at once. The action 'patch' allows updating trigger categories in bulk. Returns job status and results that can be polled for completion. Endpoint: POST /api/v2/trigger_categories/jobs

action.description: The batch action to perform on trigger categories. Currently only 'patch' is supported.

trigger_category_ids.description: List of trigger category IDs to include in the batch job

trigger_categories.jobs.create.title: Create Trigger Categories Batch Job

trigger_categories.create.description: Create a new trigger category in Zendesk. Trigger categories are used to organize and group triggers for better management. Use when setting up automated workflows or organizing business rules. This action creates a trigger category with the specified name and optional position. The name must be unique within the account.

name.description: The name of the trigger category. Names must be unique within the account.

position.description: The position of the trigger category. Triggers with lower positions are run first.

trigger_categories.create.title: Create Zendesk Trigger Category

user_fields.options.create.description: Create or update an option for a dropdown or multiselect user field. Use when you need to add a new selectable option to a custom user field of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'. If an option with the same value already exists, it will be updated with the provided name. This action is idempotent - running it multiple times with the same value will update the existing option rather than creating duplicates.

name.description: The name of the option displayed to agents and end users in the dropdown

value.description: The internal value of the option used when saving the user field selection

position.description: The relative position of the option in the dropdown list. Options with lower positions appear first.

allow_solving.description: If true, selecting this option allows the ticket to be solved when the field is required to solve

user_field_id.description: The ID or key of the user field to add the option to. The user field must be of type 'multiselect' or 'tagger'.

user_fields.options.create.title: Create User Field Option

users.identities.create.description: Tool to add an identity to a user's profile in Zendesk. An agent can add multiple identities to a user (e.g., multiple email addresses). Use this when a user needs to be contacted via a new channel or needs an additional identifier. Use when you need to add an additional identity (email, phone, social) to an existing Zendesk user.

value.description: The identifier value for this identity, such as an email address, phone number, or social media handle.

primary.description: Set to true to make this identity the primary identity for the user. Defaults to false. Note: Primary can only be set on creation, not on update.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user to add the identity to. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads (requester_id, submitter_id, assignee_id, author_id) or from user search results.

users.identities.create.title: Create User Identity

user_profiles.events.create.description: Store an event against a Sunshine user profile. Creates the profile if it doesn't exist. Use when tracking user activities such as purchases, sign-ups, or custom application events. The event is associated with the profile identified by the provided identifiers. This action is useful for building user activity timelines and triggering automations based on profile events.

event.description: Event information containing the event details and properties.

profile.description: Profile information for the user who triggered the event. The profile is created if it doesn't exist.

user_profiles.events.create.title: Create User Profile Event

users.logout_many.description: Log out multiple users in Zendesk by ending their active sessions. This action is irreversible — the affected users will be logged out and will need to re-authenticate. Use when you need to immediately terminate sessions for multiple users (e.g., after security incident, offboarding, or credential revocation). The operation accepts up to 100 user IDs at a time.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of up to 100 user IDs to log out. The IDs must belong to end-users or agents, not brands or organizations.

users.logout_many.title: Logout Many Zendesk Users

users.organization_memberships.create.description: Create a new organization membership for a specific user in Zendesk by assigning a user to an organization. Use when you need to associate an existing user with an organization so they can access organization-specific tickets and data. This action targets a specific user by their ID. This action is idempotent in that creating a duplicate membership will fail with a specific error, but the operation itself is not naturally idempotent.

default.description: Denotes whether this is the default organization membership for the user. If set to true, this membership will be the primary organization for the user. Defaults to false if not specified.

user_id.description: The ID of the user for whom to create the organization membership. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to assign the user to. Must be a non-null integer. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION_BY_ID; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

users.organization_memberships.create.title: Create User Organization Membership

users.tags.create.description: Set tags on a Zendesk user via POST request to /api/v2/users/{user_id}/tags. Use when you need to add or update tags on a specific user. Note that this replaces all existing tags on the user with the provided set of tags. This action is idempotent.

tags.description: An array of tag names to set on the user. Existing tags will be replaced with these tags.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user to set tags for

users.tags.create.title: Create Users Tags

views.create.description: Create a new view in Zendesk. Views are saved ticket filters that help agents organize and prioritize their work. They can filter tickets by conditions like status, priority, assignee, and more. Use this action when you need to: - Create a custom view for a specific team or workflow - Set up views for different ticket priorities or statuses - Create views with restricted access for specific groups - Configure views with specific columns, grouping, and sort order Note: At minimum, the 'all' conditions must include a condition checking 'status', 'type', 'group_id', 'assignee_id', or 'requester_id'.

title.description: The title of the view. Must be unique within the account.

active.description: Whether the view is active and visible to agents. Set to false to save as a draft.

output.description: Output configuration for view display settings.

conditions.description: The conditions that define which tickets appear in the view. 'all' conditions must ALL be true; 'any' conditions allow OR logic. At least one 'all' condition is required.

description.description: The description of the view shown to agents.

views.create.title: Create View

views.preview.description: Preview a Zendesk view by constructing conditions and execution settings to see which tickets match. Use when you need to test or validate view conditions before saving, or to retrieve a live preview of tickets matching specific filter criteria without creating a permanent view. This action is useful for verifying view logic, testing conditions, and previewing results before committing to a saved view.

page.description: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

view.description: The view object containing title, conditions, and execution settings to preview

columns.description: Optional list of column definitions to override or extend the view's columns in the output

exclude.description: A comma-separated list of sideloads to exclude from the response.

include.description: A comma-separated list of sideloads to include in the response.

per_page.description: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

views.preview.title: Preview View

views.preview_count.description: Preview ticket count for a view in Zendesk. Returns the number of tickets matching the specified conditions before saving the view. Use when you want to verify how many tickets will match a view's filter criteria before creating or updating a view. This action sends a POST request to /api/v2/views/preview/count with view conditions and returns the matching ticket count. Rate limited to 5 requests per minute, per view, per agent.

output.description: Output configuration for view sorting and grouping.

all_conditions.description: Array of one or more conditions that a ticket must meet ALL of to be included. This is the 'all' array in the view object. At least one condition is required. Note: 'all' is a Python keyword, so this field is named 'all_conditions' but maps to 'all' in the API.

any_conditions.description: Array of conditions where a ticket meets ANY of them to be included. Optional - if not provided, only 'all_conditions' are used. Note: 'any' is a Python keyword, so this field is named 'any_conditions' but maps to 'any' in the API.

views.preview_count.title: Preview View Ticket Count

custom_objects.create.description: Create a new custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to define a new custom object type to store and manage custom data. The key is immutable once created, so choose carefully.

custom_object.description: The custom object definition containing key, title, title_pluralized, and optional properties.

custom_objects.create.title: Create Zendesk Custom Object

custom_objects.fields.create.description: Create a new field for a custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to add a new attribute or data field to an existing custom object type. The key is immutable once created. This action is idempotent for the same key, but the key parameter must be unique per custom object.

key.description: A user-defined unique identifier for the field. Once created, this value cannot be changed.

tag.description: A tag associated with this field for filtering and organization

type.description: The data type of the field. Common types include: 'text', 'integer', 'boolean', 'float', 'date', 'datetime', 'tag', 'enumeration', 'relation'

title.description: Display name for the field shown in the Zendesk interface

active.description: Whether the field is active and available for use

position.description: Position of the field in the field list. Lower values appear first.

required.description: Whether this field is required when creating records. Omit (None) to use Zendesk's server-side default; pass True/False to set explicitly.

properties.description: Additional properties for a custom object field.

description.description: A description of the field to help agents understand its purpose

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object to add the field to

custom_field_options.description: List of options for dropdown/enumeration type fields

regexp_for_validation.description: A regular expression pattern to validate the field value against

relationship_target_type.description: For relationship fields, the key of the target custom object type

custom_objects.fields.create.title: Create Zendesk Custom Object Field

groups.create.description: Create a new group in Zendesk. The group name must be unique within the account. Use when organizing agents into teams for ticket assignment and routing. Returns the full group object including the assigned ID — persist it for subsequent operations.

name.description: The name of the group. Must be unique within the account. Leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed.

is_public.description: If true, the group is public and visible to all agents. If false, the group is private. Note: You cannot change a private group to a public group after creation.

description.description: An optional description of the group explaining its purpose or responsibilities

groups.create.title: Create Zendesk Group

tickets.import.description: Import a ticket into Zendesk with historical timestamps. This action creates tickets with past `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `solved_at` values, useful for migrating historical data. For real-time ticket creation, use ZENDESK_CREATE_ZENDESK_TICKET. Tickets created with 'closed' status and archive_immediately=true bypass normal lifecycle and go directly to archive.

tags.description: Array of tags to apply to the ticket.

due_at.description: Due date for the ticket in ISO 8601 format. Only applicable for task tickets.

subject.description: Short summary of the issue for the imported ticket.

group_id.description: The ID of the group to assign the ticket to.

email_ccs.description: Array of email CC objects for adding/removing email CCs.

followers.description: Array of follower objects for adding/removing followers.

solved_at.description: The time the ticket was solved (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

created_at.description: The time the ticket was created (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: The time the ticket was last updated (for historical imports) in ISO 8601 format.

assignee_id.description: The ID of the agent to assign to the ticket.

description.description: Long-form description / steps to reproduce. This becomes the initial comment on the ticket.

external_id.description: An external ID to link this ticket to records in another system.

requester_id.description: The ID of the user who requested this ticket.

collaborators.description: Array of collaborators to CC on the ticket. Each element can be: a user ID (integer), an email address (string), or an object with 'email' and optional 'name'.

custom_fields.description: Array of custom field objects with 'id' and 'value' properties.

collaborator_ids.description: Array of user IDs to add as collaborators (CCs) on the ticket.

custom_status_id.description: The custom ticket status id of the ticket.

archive_immediately.description: If true, any ticket created with a 'closed' status bypasses the normal ticket lifecycle and will be created directly in your ticket archive.

tickets.import.title: Import Zendesk Ticket

targets.create.description: Create a target in Zendesk for triggering outbound integrations. Use when you need to set up a notification channel or integration with external services like Campfire, email, URL webhooks, or other supported targets. Targets can be used with triggers and automation rules. Note: URL targets are being discontinued October 28, 2024 in favor of webhooks. Email targets remain unaffected.

to.description: Recipient phone number for clickatell targets.

room.description: Room name or ID for campfire targets.

address_email.description: Email address for email targets (recipient) and get_satisfaction targets (auth).

title.description: A name for the target. Must be unique within the account.

token.description: API token for basecamp, campfire, pivotal, twitter, and yammer targets.

active.description: Whether the target is active. Defaults to true. Set to false to create without activating.

group_id.description: Yammer group ID (optional for yammer targets).

attribute.description: Attribute name to send for url_target. The ticket field value will be sent as this parameter.

from_field.description: Sender phone number for clickatell targets.

project_id.description: Project ID for basecamp and pivotal targets.

target_url.description: URL for basecamp, get_satisfaction, and jira targets. Must be a valid HTTPS URL.

targets.create.title: Create Zendesk Target

channels.voice.tickets.create.description: Create a ticket in Zendesk via the voice/channel API endpoint. Use this action when you need to create tickets from phone calls, voicemails, or other voice channel interactions. Returns `ticket_id` and `ticket_url` for the created ticket. This endpoint is specifically for Zendesk Talk/voice channel ticket creation.

tags.description: Array of tags to apply to the ticket.

via_id.description: The via ID for the channel through which the ticket was created.

subject.description: Short summary of the issue. Keep it concise (e.g. 'Cannot log in' or 'Voicemail from customer').

group_id.description: The ID of the group to assign the ticket to.

assignee_id.description: The ID of the agent to assign to the ticket.

description.description: Long-form description / steps to reproduce. This becomes the initial comment on the ticket.

external_id.description: An external ID to link this ticket to records in another system.

requester_id.description: The ID of the user requesting support. If provided, requester_name and requester_email are ignored.

custom_fields.description: Array of custom field objects with 'id' and 'value' properties.

voice_comment.description: Voice comment details for voicemail tickets.

requester_name.description: Name of the requester. If you supply this, you MUST also supply `requester_email`. Leave both blank to default to the authenticated user. Ignored if requester_id is provided.

requester_email.description: Email of the requester. Must accompany `requester_name`. Ignored if requester_id is provided.

display_to_agent.description: Optional agent ID who will see the newly created ticket. Use this to route the ticket to a specific agent for immediate attention.

channels.voice.tickets.create.title: Create Ticket or Voicemail Ticket

user_fields.create.description: Create a custom user field in Zendesk. Use when you need to define a new custom field to capture additional user data. Supports text, checkbox, dropdown, multiselect, date, integer, decimal, regexp validation, and lookup types. Only administrators can create user fields.

key.description: Unique key that identifies this custom field. Must contain only letters, numbers, and underscores. Cannot be only numbers.

title.description: The title (label) displayed for this custom field

active.description: If true, this field is available for use. Defaults to true.

position.description: Ordering of the field relative to other user fields

raw_title.description: Dynamic content placeholder for title (supports i18n placeholders)

description.description: User-defined description of this field's purpose

raw_description.description: Dynamic content placeholder for description (supports i18n placeholders)

relationship_filter.description: Filter definition for autocomplete results in lookup fields.

custom_field_options.description: Required for 'dropdown' and 'multiselect' types. Each option has a name (display) and value (internal tag).

regexp_for_validation.description: Regular expression pattern for validation. Required for 'regexp' type fields.

user_fields.create.title: Create Zendesk User Field

custom_objects.access_rules.delete.description: Delete an access rule for a custom object in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the access rule cannot be recovered once deleted. Use when you need to remove access control rules for custom objects.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object

custom_objects.access_rules.delete.title: Delete Access Rule

automations.delete.description: Permanently deletes an automation in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the automation will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete automations or removing test data. **Note**: You might be restricted from deleting automations that are active or referenced by other rules.

automation_id.description: The ID of the automation to delete

automations.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Automation

business_hours.schedules.delete.description: Permanently deletes a business hours schedule in Zendesk. Use when you need to remove obsolete schedules or clean up test data. This action is irreversible — the schedule cannot be recovered once removed. Admin permissions are required. **Note**: Schedules that are currently in use by active SLA policies or other configurations may not be deletable.

schedule_id.description: The ID of the schedule to delete

business_hours.schedules.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Business Hours Schedule

custom_objects.records.attachments.delet.description: Permanently deletes an attachment from a custom object record in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific file attachment from a custom object record. This action is irreversible — the attachment will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. **Note**: Only attachments that are not required and not the primary attachment can be deleted.

id.description: The ID of the custom object record attachment to delete

record_id.description: The ID of the custom object record that contains the attachment to delete

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object that contains the record with the attachment

custom_objects.records.attachments.delet.title: Delete Custom Object Record Attachment

custom_objects.records.delete_by_externa.description: Permanently deletes a custom object record in Zendesk by its external ID or name. Use this action when you need to remove a specific record from a custom object. This action is irreversible — the record cannot be recovered once deleted. Requires admin permissions. **Note**: Either external_id or name must be provided to identify the record to delete.

name.description: The name of the custom object record to delete. Use either external_id or name to identify the record.

external_id.description: The external ID of the custom object record to delete. Use either external_id or name to identify the record.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object containing the record to delete

custom_objects.records.delete_by_externa.title: Delete Custom Object Record

deleted_tickets.delete.description: Permanently deletes a soft-deleted ticket from Zendesk. This action is irreversible - once a ticket is permanently deleted, it cannot be recovered. Use this action to remove tickets that were previously soft-deleted using the delete_ticket action. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a ticket that has already been deleted and is no longer accessible through normal operations.

ticket_id.description: The ID of the deleted ticket to permanently remove

deleted_tickets.delete.title: Delete Deleted Ticket Permanently

deletion_schedules.delete.description: Permanently deletes a deletion schedule in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the deletion schedule will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete deletion schedules or removing test data.

deletion_schedule_id.description: The ID of the deletion schedule to delete

deletion_schedules.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Deletion Schedule

group_memberships.delete.description: Permanently deletes a group membership in Zendesk, immediately removing a user from a group. This action is irreversible — the group membership cannot be recovered once deleted. Use when cleaning up obsolete group memberships or removing users from groups. **Note**: Deleting a group membership does not delete the user or the group itself, only the association between them.

group_membership_id.description: The ID of the group membership to delete

group_memberships.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Group Membership

group_memberships.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete group memberships in Zendesk. Immediately removes users from groups. This action is irreversible — the memberships will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up test data or removing obsolete group memberships in one call. Returns a job_status payload; deletions complete asynchronously.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk group membership IDs to delete. Example: 26923118307484,26923118307485,26923118307486

group_memberships.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Group Memberships

macros.delete.description: Permanently deletes a macro in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the macro will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete macros or removing test data. **Note**: You might be restricted from deleting macros that are active or referenced by other rules.

macro_id.description: The ID of the macro to delete

macros.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Macro

macros.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete macros in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the macros will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete macros or removing test data.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk macro IDs to delete

macros.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Macros

automations.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete automations in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the automations will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete automations or removing test data.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk automation IDs to delete

automations.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Automations

object_triggers.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete triggers for a Zendesk custom object. This action is irreversible — the triggers will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete triggers or removing test data for a specific custom object. Returns a success indicator upon completion. Requires the custom object key and a comma-separated list of trigger IDs to identify which triggers to delete.

ids.description: A comma separated list of trigger IDs to delete

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object

object_triggers.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Custom Object Triggers

organization_memberships.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete organization memberships in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the memberships will be permanently removed and cannot be recovered once deleted. Use when cleaning up obsolete organization memberships or removing users from organizations. Returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling to confirm completion.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk organization membership IDs to delete

organization_memberships.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Organization Memberships

views.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete views in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the views will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete views or removing test data. Returns 204 No Content on success.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk view IDs to delete

views.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Views

organization_fields.delete.description: Permanently deletes an organization field in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a custom organization field from the system. This action is irreversible — the organization field will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Any data stored in this field across all organizations will be lost. **Note**: Ensure no organizations are using this field before deletion, as the deletion cannot be undone.

organization_field_id.description: The ID or key of the organization field to delete

organization_fields.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Organization Field

organization_memberships.delete.description: Permanently removes a user from an organization in Zendesk by deleting the organization membership. This action is irreversible — the membership cannot be recovered once deleted. Use this action when you need to remove a user's association with an organization. This operation requires admin permissions.

organization_membership_id.description: The ID of the organization membership to delete

organization_memberships.delete.title: Delete Organization Membership

organization_subscriptions.delete.description: Permanently deletes an organization subscription in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the subscription cannot be recovered once removed. Use when you need to remove an organization subscription.

organization_subscription_id.description: The ID of the organization subscription to delete

organization_subscriptions.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Organization Subscription

resource_collections.delete.description: Delete a resource collection in Zendesk. Use when you need to remove a resource collection that is no longer needed. This action returns a job status that can be polled to track the deletion progress. This operation is irreversible; confirm the correct resource_collection_id before executing.

resource_collection_id.description: The ID of the resource collection to delete

resource_collections.delete.title: Delete Resource Collection

suspended_tickets.destroy_many.description: Permanently deletes multiple suspended tickets in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the suspended tickets will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up spam or irrelevant suspended tickets. Accepts up to 100 ticket IDs per request.

ids.description: A comma-separated list of suspended ticket IDs to delete (max 100)

suspended_tickets.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Suspended Tickets

targets.delete.description: Permanently deletes a target in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the target will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete targets or removing test data. **Note**: Deleting a target that is actively used by triggers or other automation rules may cause those rules to fail.

target_id.description: The ID of the target to delete

targets.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Target

ticket_fields.delete.description: Permanently deletes a ticket field in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a custom ticket field that is no longer needed. This action is irreversible — the ticket field and all associated data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires admin permissions. **Note**: System ticket fields cannot be deleted. Only custom ticket fields can be removed.

creator.description: If true, displays the `creator_user_id` and `creator_app_name` properties in the response. If the ticket field is created by an app, `creator_app_name` is the name of the app and `creator_user_id` is -1. If the ticket field is not created by an app, then `creator_app_name` is null

ticket_field_id.description: The ID of the ticket field to delete

ticket_fields.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Ticket Field

ticket_fields.options.delete.description: Permanently deletes an option from a ticket field in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific selectable option from a dropdown or multiselect ticket field. This action is irreversible — the ticket field option will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. **Note**: Only custom options can be deleted. System-defined options cannot be removed.

ticket_field_id.description: The ID of the ticket field containing the option to delete

ticket_field_option_id.description: The ID of the ticket field option to delete

ticket_fields.options.delete.title: Delete Ticket Field Option

triggers.delete.description: Permanently deletes a trigger in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the trigger will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete triggers or removing test data. **Note**: You might be restricted from deleting triggers that are active or referenced by other rules.

trigger_id.description: The ID of the trigger to delete

triggers.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Trigger

trigger_categories.delete.description: Permanently deletes a trigger category in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the trigger category will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when cleaning up obsolete trigger categories or removing test data. **Note**: You might be restricted from deleting trigger categories that are in use by active triggers.

trigger_category_id.description: The ID of the ticket trigger category to delete

trigger_categories.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Trigger Category

user_fields.delete.description: Permanently deletes a user field in Zendesk, removing it from all user profiles. This action is irreversible — the field and all its associated data will be permanently lost. Use when cleaning up deprecated custom fields or removing test fields.

user_field_id.description: The ID or key of the user field to delete

user_fields.delete.title: Delete Zendesk User Field

user_fields.options.delete.description: Permanently deletes an option from a user field in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific selectable option from a dropdown or multiselect user field. This action is irreversible — the user field option will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed.

user_field_id.description: The ID or key of the user field containing the option to delete

user_field_option_id.description: The ID of the user field option to delete

user_fields.options.delete.title: Delete User Field Option

deleted_users.delete.description: Permanently deletes a soft-deleted user from Zendesk. This action is irreversible - once a user is permanently deleted, it cannot be recovered. Use this action to remove users that were previously soft-deleted using the delete_user action. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a user that has already been deleted and is no longer accessible through normal operations. This action requires appropriate admin permissions.

deleted_user_id.description: The ID of the deleted user to permanently remove

deleted_users.delete.title: Permanently Delete User

user_profiles.delete.description: Permanently deletes a user profile in Zendesk by its profile ID. This action is irreversible — the profile and all associated data will be permanently lost. Use when cleaning up duplicate profiles, test profiles, or removing profiles that are no longer needed. Requires agent-level access with appropriate role permissions.

profile_id.description: The Sunshine profile ID of the user profile to delete

user_profiles.delete.title: Delete Zendesk User Profile

users.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete users from Zendesk by their IDs or external IDs. This action is irreversible — once deleted, users cannot be recovered. Use when cleaning up test data, removing obsolete accounts, or consolidating user records in bulk. The operation returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling via the job_status URL to confirm completion.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk user IDs to delete (max 100). Required if external_ids is not provided.

external_ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk external user IDs to delete (max 100). Required if ids is not provided.

users.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Users

users.sessions.delete.description: Delete a specific user session in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to invalidate and remove a specific user session. This action is irreversible — the session cannot be recovered once deleted. Use when you need to forcibly log out a user or remove a specific session from their account for security or administrative purposes.

user_id.description: The ID of the user

session_id.description: The ID of the session to delete

users.sessions.delete.title: Delete Zendesk User Session

users.group_memberships.delete.description: Permanently deletes a user's group membership in Zendesk, immediately removing a user from a group. This action is irreversible — the group membership cannot be recovered once deleted. Use when cleaning up obsolete group memberships, removing users from groups, or revoking group access. **Note**: Deleting a group membership does not delete the user or the group itself, only the association between them. The user will no longer have access to tickets routed to that group.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user whose group membership to delete

group_membership_id.description: The numeric ID of the group membership to delete

users.group_memberships.delete.title: Delete Zendesk User's Group Membership

users.identities.delete.description: Deletes an identity for a given user in Zendesk. Use when you need to remove a specific identity (e.g., email, phone, social login) from a user's account. This action is irreversible — once the identity is deleted, it cannot be recovered. Ensure you have the correct user_id and user_identity_id before executing.

user_id.description: The ID of the user

user_identity_id.description: The ID of the user identity to delete

users.identities.delete.title: Delete User Identity

users.me.logout.description: Delete the current authenticated session in Zendesk. This action invalidates the current API session, requiring re-authentication for future API calls. Use when you need to explicitly log out the current user session or terminate an active authenticated connection. This action is irreversible — the session cannot be recovered once deleted. Note: This action targets the authenticated user's own session only and cannot terminate other user sessions.
users.me.logout.title: Delete Authenticated Session

users.organization_memberships.delete.description: Permanently removes a user from an organization in Zendesk by deleting the organization membership for a specific user. This action is irreversible — the membership cannot be recovered once deleted. Use this action when you need to remove a user's association with an organization for a specific user. This operation requires admin permissions.

user_id.description: The ID of the user

organization_membership_id.description: The ID of the organization membership to delete

users.organization_memberships.delete.title: Delete User's Organization Membership

users.sessions.delete_all.description: Bulk delete all sessions for a specific user in Zendesk. This action invalidates all active sessions for the specified user, forcing them to re-authenticate on their next API call or login. Use when you need to forcibly log out a user by revoking all their active sessions, such as during security incidents or account deactivation. This action is irreversible — all sessions for the user will be immediately invalidated and cannot be recovered.

user_id.description: The ID of the user whose sessions to delete

users.sessions.delete_all.title: Delete All User Sessions

views.delete.description: Delete a single view in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the view will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Use when you need to remove a specific obsolete view or test view. Returns 204 No Content on success.

view_id.description: The ID of the view to delete

views.delete.title: Delete Zendesk View

apps.installations.delete.description: Permanently removes an installed app from Zendesk. Use when you need to uninstall an app from your Zendesk instance. This action is irreversible — the app installation cannot be recovered once removed. Admin permissions are required.

app_installation_id.description: The ID of the app installation to delete

apps.installations.delete.title: Delete Zendesk App Installation

bookmarks.delete.description: Permanently deletes a bookmark in Zendesk. Use when you need to remove a user bookmark. This action is irreversible — the bookmark cannot be recovered once deleted.

bookmark_id.description: The ID of the bookmark to delete

bookmarks.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Bookmark

custom_objects.delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom object definition in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a custom object type and all its associated records. This action is irreversible — the custom object and all its data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires admin permissions. **Note**: Deleting a custom object will also delete all records associated with it.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object to delete

custom_objects.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Custom Object

custom_objects.fields.delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom object field in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific field from a custom object definition. This action is irreversible — the field and all its data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires admin permissions.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object that contains the field to delete

custom_object_field_key_or_id.description: The key or ID of the custom object field to delete

custom_objects.fields.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Custom Object Field

custom_objects.records.delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom object record in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific record from a custom object type. This action is irreversible — the record and its data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires the custom object key and the record ID to identify which specific record to delete.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object containing the record to delete

custom_object_record_id.description: The ID of the custom object record to delete

custom_objects.records.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Custom Object Record

custom_statuses.delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom ticket status in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a custom ticket status from the system. This action is irreversible — the custom status will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. **Note**: Ensure no tickets are using this custom status before deletion.

custom_status_id.description: The ID of the custom ticket status to delete

custom_statuses.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Custom Status

dynamic_content.delete.description: Permanently deletes a dynamic content item in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the dynamic content item cannot be recovered once deleted. Always confirm the correct dynamic_content_item_id before executing.

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The ID of the dynamic content item to delete

dynamic_content.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Dynamic Content Item

dynamic_content.variants.delete.description: Permanently deletes a dynamic content item variant in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the variant cannot be recovered once deleted. Always confirm the correct dynamic_content_item_id and dynamic_content_variant_id before executing.

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The ID of the dynamic content item containing the variant to delete

dynamic_content_variant_id.description: The ID of the variant to delete

dynamic_content.variants.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Dynamic Content Item Variant

object_triggers.delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom object trigger in Zendesk. Use this action when you need to remove a specific trigger from a custom object definition. This action is irreversible — the trigger and all its data will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered once removed. Requires admin permissions.

trigger_id.description: The ID of the trigger to delete

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object that contains the trigger to delete

object_triggers.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Custom Object Trigger

recipient_addresses.delete.description: Permanently deletes a support address from Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the support address cannot be recovered once deleted. Use this action when you need to remove a deprecated or unwanted support email address from your Zendesk account. This operation requires admin permissions and the support address must not be set as the default address. Deleting an address that is actively used may impact email routing.

support_address_id.description: The ID of the support address to delete

recipient_addresses.delete.title: Delete Zendesk Support Address

deleted_tickets.destroy_many.description: Permanently deletes multiple soft-deleted tickets in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the tickets will be permanently removed and cannot be recovered once executed. Use when cleaning up test tickets or removing obsolete soft-deleted tickets in bulk. The operation returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling to confirm completion. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to permanently delete (max 100). Only soft-deleted tickets can be destroyed.

deleted_tickets.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Soft-Deleted Zendesk Tickets

organizations.destroy_many.description: Bulk delete Zendesk organizations. This action is irreversible - once organizations are deleted, they cannot be recovered. Use when you need to remove multiple organizations in a single operation. Returns a job_status payload (initial status typically 'queued'); deletions complete asynchronously and may require follow-up polling to confirm completion. Maximum 100 organizations per request. Use this action when you need to clean up test data, remove obsolete organizations, or perform bulk organization deletions. You must provide either 'ids' (comma-separated list of Zendesk organization IDs) or 'external_ids' (comma-separated list of external IDs).

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk organization IDs to delete (max 100). Required if external_ids is not provided.

external_ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk external organization IDs to delete (max 100). Required if ids is not provided.

organizations.destroy_many.title: Bulk Delete Zendesk Organizations

locales.detect_best.description: Detect the best language/locale for the current user based on their browser settings and account preferences. Use when you need to determine the optimal language to display content in for a user, such as when localizing ticket comments, article content, or Help Center pages. This action reads the user's preferred languages from the Accept-Language header and matches them against supported locales in your Zendesk account. The detected locale is returned with full locale details including ID, name, and API URL.
locales.detect_best.title: Detect Best Locale

account.settings.get.description: Retrieve Zendesk account settings. Use this action when you need to view the configuration and feature flags for a Zendesk account, including API settings, branding, ticket preferences, chat configuration, voice settings, and more.

authenticity_token.description: Legacy CSRF token. Ignored by API.

account.settings.get.title: Get Account Settings

triggers.list_active.description: List all active ticket triggers in Zendesk. Use when you need to retrieve the currently active trigger rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. This action returns all triggers marked as active, including their conditions, actions, and metadata. Active triggers are business rules that define what happens when ticket conditions are satisfied. This is useful for auditing active automation rules, understanding automated workflows, or finding specific trigger configurations.

page.description: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: traditional uses `?page=2` (integer page number); cursor uses `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). Mutually exclusive.

sort.description: Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'position'.

sort_by.description: Offset pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'usage_1h', 'usage_24h', or 'usage_7d'. Defaults to 'position'

per_page.description: Number of records to return per page. Maximum is 100 records per page for the active-triggers endpoint.

sort_order.description: One of 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sort, 'desc' for all others

triggers.list_active.title: List Active Triggers

activities.count.description: Count ticket activities in Zendesk. Returns an approximate count of ticket activities. Use when you need to know how many activities exist in the activity stream for reporting or operational purposes.
activities.count.title: Count Activities

apps.get.description: Get a single Zendesk app by its numeric ID. Use when you have an app ID and need to retrieve the app's details including name, author information, version, installation count, categories, and description.

app_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app to retrieve.

apps.get.title: Get App

apps.installations.requirements.description: List all requirements for a Zendesk app installation. Use when you need to check what configuration or parameters are required for a specific installed app to function properly. Requirements may include OAuth settings, parameter configurations, or other setup steps needed by the app. This action is read-only and idempotent.

app_installation_id.description: The numeric ID of the app installation to retrieve requirements for. You can find this ID from the app installations list or when working with specific app installations.

apps.installations.requirements.title: Get App Installation Requirements

apps.locations.get.description: Get details for a specific Zendesk app location by its numeric ID. Returns location properties including visibility settings, orderability, and associated product codes. Use when you have an app_location_id from listing locations or creating apps and need to retrieve detailed location information. Only accessible to admin users.

app_location_id.description: The numeric ID of the app location to retrieve. This is the internal location ID returned by Zendesk when listing or creating app locations.

apps.locations.get.title: Get App Location

apps.location_installations.list.description: List all apps location installations from Zendesk. Returns an array of app installation IDs organized by location name. Use when you need to retrieve information about apps installed in specific locations within Zendesk, such as nav_bar or other supported locations. This action is read-only and idempotent. Allowed for: Admins only.
apps.location_installations.list.title: List Apps Location Installations

apps.public_key.get.description: Retrieves the public key for a specific Zendesk app. The response is in JSON Web Key (JWK) format containing RSA key components (modulus n, exponent e). Use this action when you need to verify JWTs issued by a Zendesk app or establish trust for app-based authentication. This is a read-only operation.

app_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app whose public key you want to retrieve.

apps.public_key.get.title: Get App Public Key

attachments.get.description: Retrieve details of a single Zendesk attachment by its ID. Use when you have an attachment_id from ticket comments or an attachments list and need to fetch full attachment metadata including file name, size, content type, URLs, and thumbnails. The action returns the attachment object with all available properties.

attachment_id.description: The numeric ID of the attachment to retrieve. You can find attachment IDs in ticket comments or via the attachments list endpoint.

attachments.get.title: Get Attachment

tags.autocomplete_get.description: Search for Zendesk tags using autocomplete. Use when you need to find tag suggestions based on a partial tag name for tagging tickets or organizing content.

name.description: A substring of a tag name to search for. The API returns registered and recent tags matching this substring.

tags.autocomplete_get.title: Get Autocomplete Tags

automations.get.description: Show a specific automation by its ID. Use when you need to retrieve details of a single automation rule in your Zendesk account, such as for auditing, modifying, or understanding what actions and conditions are configured for a particular automation. This action is read-only and idempotent.

automation_id.description: The ID of the automation to retrieve

automations.get.title: Show Automation

automations.list.description: List all automations for the current Zendesk account. Use when you need to retrieve, audit, or review the automation rules configured in your Zendesk account. Automations are business rules that automatically perform actions based on trigger conditions. Supports both traditional offset pagination and cursor-based pagination. Filter by active status to show only enabled or disabled automations.

page.description: Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination: Traditional: `?page=2` (integer page number). Cursor: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` (deepObject with size, after, before). These are mutually exclusive - use one format or the other, not both.

sort.description: Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering. Example: `?sort=name` or `?sort=-created_at`

active.description: Filter by active automations if true or inactive automations if false

include.description: A sideload to include in the response. See Zendesk API documentation for available sideloads.

per_page.description: Number of records to return per page. Default and maximum values vary by endpoint.

automations.list.title: List Automations

automations.search.description: Search for Zendesk automations by their title. Use when you need to find automations in your Zendesk account by searching for keywords in their titles. Automations are business rules that automatically perform actions when certain conditions are met. This action supports filtering by active status and sorting results.

query.description: Query string used to find all automations with matching title. Case-insensitive partial match on automation titles.

active.description: Filter automations by active status. Set to true to return only active automations, or false to return only inactive automations. When not specified, returns both active and inactive automations.

include.description: Sideload related data to include in the response. Currently supported: 'usage_24h' returns statistics about how many times each automation was triggered in the last 24 hours.

automations.search.title: Search Automations

brands.list.description: List all brands configured in your Zendesk account.
