user_identity_id.description: The ID of the user identity to make primary

users.identities.make_primary.title: Make User Identity Primary

tickets.mark_many_as_spam.description: Marks multiple tickets as spam in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the tickets will be marked as spam and moved to the suspended tickets queue. The submitter will also be marked as spam and blocked from submitting further tickets. Use when cleaning up spam or unwanted tickets to protect your support queue. Returns a job_status payload for tracking the bulk operation. Note: Tickets marked as spam are moved to the suspended tickets queue and cannot be recovered through normal means.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to mark as spam. Maximum 100 IDs allowed per request.

tickets.mark_many_as_spam.title: Mark Multiple Tickets as Spam

users.merge.description: Merges two Zendesk end users together. The user specified in the path parameter (user_id) is the primary user (target) that will be kept. The user specified in the request body (id) is the source user that will be deleted and its data transferred to the primary user. Use when you need to consolidate duplicate end-user accounts in Zendesk. This action is irreversible — the source user and all their associated data (tickets, comments, etc.) will be merged into the primary user and the source user cannot be recovered.

user.description: User object containing the ID of the user to merge from. The 'id' field is mandatory - the source user will be deleted. The 'name' field is optional to rename the primary user.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the primary user (target) to merge another user into

users.merge.title: Merge Users

users.open.description: Open a Zendesk user's profile in a specified agent's browser. Use when an agent needs to view a specific user's profile during an active call or session. This action triggers the Zendesk Talk dashboard to display the user's information in the agent's interface.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose profile should be displayed in the agent's browser. You can find this in the user's profile URL or from user search results.

agent_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk agent whose browser should display the user profile. You can find this in the agent's profile URL or from agent listings.

users.open.title: Open User's Profile in Agent Browser

suspended_tickets.recover_many.description: Recover multiple suspended tickets in Zendesk. Use when you need to restore tickets that have been suspended (e.g., auto-replied emails, bounced messages). Takes up to 100 ticket IDs as input and restores them to normal ticket status. This action is irreversible — recovered tickets return to normal processing.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of suspended ticket IDs to recover (max 100). Use the auto-generated numeric IDs.

suspended_tickets.recover_many.title: Recover Multiple Suspended Tickets

users.me.session.renew.description: Renew the current Zendesk session and obtain a new authenticity token. Use when the current session token is expiring or needs to be refreshed to maintain an active authenticated connection. This action extends the session lifetime without requiring full re-authentication.
users.me.session.renew.title: Renew Session

custom_objects.fields.reorder.description: Reorder Custom Fields of an Object. Updates the display order of custom object fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of fields displayed in a custom object's record layout. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

custom_object_field_ids.description: An array of custom object field IDs specifying the new order. The order of IDs in the array determines the display order of the fields.

custom_objects.fields.reorder.title: Reorder Custom Object Fields

apps.location_installations.reorder.description: Reorder App Installations For Location. Creates or updates the relevant location installation with a specified installation order. This action requires admin-level access. Use when you need to change the display order of apps in a specific Zendesk location (e.g., nav bar, ticket sidebar).

installations.description: An array of app installation IDs in the desired order. The order of IDs determines the display order in that location.

location_name.description: The location name where the installations are located. Common values: 'nav_bar', 'ticket_sidebar', 'user_sidebar', 'organization_sidebar', 'new_ticket_sidebar'.

apps.location_installations.reorder.title: Reorder App Location Installations

organization_fields.reorder.description: Reorder Organization Fields. Updates the display order of organization fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of organization fields displayed in Zendesk. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

organization_field_ids.description: An array of organization field IDs specifying the new order. The order of IDs in the array determines the display order of the fields in the organization field list.

organization_fields.reorder.title: Reorder Organization Fields

ticket_fields.reorder.description: Reorder Ticket Fields. Updates the display order of ticket fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of standard ticket fields displayed in the ticket form. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result. This action requires admin permissions.

ticket_field_ids.description: An array of ticket field IDs specifying the new display order. The order of IDs in the array determines the order of the fields. Only those provided are assigned to first positions; missing IDs get incremental positions automatically.

ticket_fields.reorder.title: Reorder Ticket Fields

triggers.reorder.description: Reorder Ticket Triggers. Updates the firing order of ticket triggers based on the provided trigger IDs. Use when you need to change the priority or execution order of ticket triggers in your Zendesk account. Important constraints: You must include EVERY ticket trigger ID in your account. Omitting any trigger ID returns 404 Forbidden. Additionally, reordering is not permitted if you have more than one ticket trigger category (returns LimitOneCategory error). This action is idempotent - re-running with the same trigger IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

trigger_ids.description: An array of ticket trigger IDs in the desired firing order. The order of IDs in the array determines the execution order. You must include every ticket trigger ID in your account - omitting any trigger ID returns 404 Forbidden.

triggers.reorder.title: Reorder Ticket Triggers

user_fields.reorder.description: Reorder User Fields. Updates the display order of custom user fields based on the provided field IDs. Use when you need to change the order of user fields displayed in user profiles or forms. This action requires admin-level access. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same field IDs in the same order will produce the same result.

user_field_ids.description: An array of user field IDs specifying the new display order. The order of IDs in the array determines the position of each field.

user_fields.reorder.title: Reorder User Fields

end_users.identities.request_verificatio.description: Send a verification email to an end user to verify ownership of their email address identity. The end user receives an email with a link to confirm their identity. Use when you need to verify an end user's email address identity in Zendesk, such as when creating new end users or resolving identity verification issues. Note: This action can only be performed by verified end users.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the end user

user_identity_id.description: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify

end_users.identities.request_verificatio.title: Request End User Verification

users.request_create.description: Send a request to create a user in Zendesk. This sends the owner a reminder email to update their user profile information. Use when you want to prompt a user to complete their profile through the request flow rather than creating directly. This action is useful for onboarding flows where you want to collect user information through an email-based request rather than creating the user directly.

user.description: User object containing attributes for the user request. The `name` field is mandatory. This action sends the owner a reminder email to complete their user profile.

users.request_create.title: Request User Create

users.identities.request_verification.description: Send a verification email to a user to verify ownership of their email address identity. The user receives an email with a link to confirm their identity. Use when you need to verify a user's email address identity in Zendesk, such as when creating new users or resolving identity verification issues. Note: This action sends a verification email to the user's identity address.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user

user_identity_id.description: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify

users.identities.request_verification.title: Request User Verification

deleted_tickets.restore_many.description: Restores multiple previously deleted tickets in Zendesk. Use when you need to recover tickets that were deleted and need to be restored in bulk. This action is reversible - tickets can be deleted again after restoration. Note: Only tickets in 'deleted' status can be restored.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk ticket IDs to restore. Example: '1,2,3' to restore tickets with IDs 1, 2, and 3. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

deleted_tickets.restore_many.title: Restore Multiple Deleted Tickets

deleted_tickets.restore.description: Restores a previously deleted ticket in Zendesk. Use when a ticket was accidentally deleted and needs to be recovered. The restored ticket will return to its previous state with all associated data intact. This action is reversible — tickets can be deleted again after restoration if needed.

ticket_id.description: ID of the deleted ticket to restore.

deleted_tickets.restore.title: Restore Zendesk Ticket

custom_objects.records.search.description: Search and filter custom object records in Zendesk using text queries and field filters. Returns paginated results with cursor-based navigation. Use when you need to find specific records within a custom object type, apply text searches or structured filters, and navigate through large result sets. This is a read-only operation. This action is useful for discovering records, running filtered queries on custom objects, and implementing paginated browsing through custom object data.

sort.description: "updated_at"

query.description: Search text-based fields for records matching specific terms. Supports fuzzy search on Text, Multi Line Text, and RegExp fields. Multiple words or numbers can be searched (e.g., 'Tesla Honda 2020' matches records containing any of these terms).

filter.description: Filter object to narrow down search results based on specific field conditions. Structure depends on the custom object's field definitions.

page_size.description: Number of records to return per page (max 100).

page_after.description: Pagination cursor for fetching records after a given point. Use 'meta.after_cursor' from a previous response. Cannot be used with page[before].

page_before.description: Pagination cursor for fetching records before a given point. Use 'meta.before_cursor' from a previous response. Cannot be used with page[after].

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car', 'test_car'). Use ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_CUSTOM_OBJECTS to discover available custom object keys.

custom_objects.records.search.title: Search Custom Object Records

help_center.articles.search.description: Search localized Zendesk Help Center articles by text and filters.

page.description: Offset page number, starting at 1.

query.description: Text to match in Help Center articles.

locale.description: Enabled locale to search, such as 'en-us', or '*' for every locale.

section.description: One or more comma-separated section IDs.

brand_id.description: Brand ID to search, as a string.

category.description: One or more comma-separated category IDs.

per_page.description: Number of results to return per page, from 1 to 100.

multibrand.description: Search all brands when true and brand_id is omitted.

label_names.description: Comma-separated article labels. An article matching any label is returned.

help_center.articles.search.title: Search Help Center Articles

object_triggers.search.description: Search for triggers associated with a custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to find triggers based on their title, description, or active status within a specific custom object. This is useful for auditing, managing, or reviewing automation rules for custom objects. Supports both cursor-based pagination (using 'sort' parameter) and offset pagination (using 'sort_by' parameter). Filter by 'active' to show only enabled or disabled triggers.

sort.description: Cursor-based pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', or 'position'.

query.description: Query string used to find all triggers with matching title

active.description: Filter by active triggers if true or inactive triggers if false

filter.description: JSON-encoded trigger attribute filters for the search. Example: {"json":{"description":"Close a ticket"}}

include.description: A sideload to include in the response

sort_by.description: Offset pagination only. Possible values are 'alphabetical', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'usage_1h', 'usage_24h', or 'usage_7d'. Defaults to 'position'

sort_order.description: One of 'asc' or 'desc'. Defaults to 'asc' for alphabetical and position sort, 'desc' for all others

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object to search triggers for

object_triggers.search.title: Search Object Triggers

custom_statuses.set_default.description: Sets one or more custom ticket statuses as the default for their respective categories. Use this action when you need to specify which custom status should be the default (fallback) status for a given category (open, pending, solved, etc.). This operation is idempotent — running it multiple times with the same IDs will produce the same result. **Allowed for**: Admins only. **Note**: The IDs should be valid custom ticket status IDs that exist in your Zendesk account.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of custom status IDs to set as default for their respective categories. Each custom status will become the default for its status category (e.g., open, pending, solved).

custom_statuses.set_default.title: Set Default Custom Ticket Status

users.group_memberships.make_default.description: Set a group membership as the default for a specific user in Zendesk. Use when you need to mark a user's group membership as the default, meaning tickets assigned directly to the agent will assume this membership's group. Requires both the user ID and the group membership ID. This action is useful for managing default routing preferences for agents in your Zendesk instance. Note that only one group membership can be the default at a time - setting a new default will automatically unset the previous default.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user. This is the user ID, not a membership ID.

group_membership_id.description: The numeric ID of the group membership to set as default. This is the group membership ID, not a group ID.

users.group_memberships.make_default.title: Set Group Membership as Default

users.organizations.make_default.description: Set an organization as the default for a user in Zendesk. Use when you need to change which organization is the primary/default for a user by specifying the organization ID directly. Only one organization can be the default at a time. This action is idempotent - setting the same organization as default multiple times will succeed without side effects.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk user whose default organization to set. Obtain from ZENDESK_LIST_USERS or ZENDESK_SEARCH_USERS; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

organization_id.description: The numeric ID of the organization to set as the user's default. Obtain from ZENDESK_GET_ALL_ORGANISATIONS or ZENDESK_GET_ZENDESK_ORGANIZATION; do not guess or fabricate IDs.

users.organizations.make_default.title: Set Organization as Default for User

custom_objects.access_rules.get.description: Show a custom object access rule by its ID. Use when you have a custom_object_key and access_rule_id and need to retrieve the access rule's details including its conditions, title, description, and timestamps. This is a read-only operation that does not modify any data. This action is useful for reviewing access control rules applied to custom objects in Zendesk.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object

custom_objects.access_rules.get.title: Show Access Rule

custom_objects.get.description: Get details of a specific Zendesk custom object by its key. Use when you have a custom object key and need to retrieve its metadata including name, description, attachment settings, visibility settings, and creation/update timestamps. This is a read-only, idempotent operation that returns the full custom object definition.

include_ui_path.description: Include UI path in the response. Set to true to retrieve the direct link to the custom object in the Zendesk UI.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

include_permissions_metadata.description: Include permission metadata in the response. Set to true to retrieve additional permission information for the custom object.

custom_objects.get.title: Show Custom Object

custom_objects.records.get.description: Get details of a specific Zendesk custom object record by its key and record ID. Use when you have a custom object key and record ID and need to retrieve the record's metadata including name, custom fields, timestamps, and photo. This is a read-only, idempotent operation that returns the full custom object record definition. Photo is only available if `allows_photos` is enabled on the custom object.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

custom_object_record_id.description: The id of a custom object record. This is the unique identifier for a specific record within the custom object.

custom_objects.records.get.title: Show Custom Object Record

job_statuses.show_many.description: Show many job statuses by their IDs in Zendesk. Use this action when you have multiple job status IDs from bulk operations (like ticket updates, user merges, or ticket merges) and need to check their status in a single request. Each ID in the comma-separated list will return its corresponding job status object if found. Endpoint: GET /api/v2/job_statuses/show_many

ids.description: Comma-separated list of job status IDs to retrieve. Each id is a 32-char hex token returned by the original async job submission response.

job_statuses.show_many.title: Show Many Job Statuses

custom_objects.permission_policies.get.description: Get details of a specific permission policy for a Zendesk custom object by its ID. Use when you have a custom_object_key and permission policy ID and need to retrieve the policy's details including the role name and record operation permissions (create, read, update, delete). This is a read-only, idempotent operation that does not modify any data. This action is useful for reviewing permission policies that control access to custom object records in Zendesk.

id.description: The permission policy ID. Use format 'custom-role-{custom_role_id}' for custom roles (e.g., 'custom-role-6678128886399') or 'end-user' for the end user system role.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

custom_objects.permission_policies.get.title: Show Permission Policy

users.organizations.delete.description: Immediately removes a user from an organization in Zendesk. Use when you need to unassign a user from an organization membership. This action is irreversible - the user will no longer be associated with the organization.

user_id.description: The ID of the user

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization

users.organizations.delete.title: Unassign User from Organization

custom_objects.access_rules.update.description: Update an existing access rule for a custom object in Zendesk. Access rules control which records of a custom object users can access based on conditions. Use this action when you need to: - Change an access rule's title or description - Modify the conditions that determine when the rule applies - Update access permissions for custom object records This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The title of the access rule

conditions.description: Conditions object for access rules - defines when the rule applies.

description.description: A description of what this access rule does

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object

custom_objects.access_rules.update.title: Update Access Rule

apps.installations.update.description: Update an app installation in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify app installation settings such as enabling/disabling the app, restricting access by groups or roles, or updating app-specific settings.

enabled.description: If true, the app installation is enabled. Set to false to disable the app for all users.

settings.description: Installation settings for the app, formatted as a flat key-value object. These are app-specific configuration values.

settings_objects.description: Installation settings for the app, formatted as an array of objects. Each object should have a 'key' and 'value' field.

role_restrictions.description: List of role names (as strings) that are allowed to use the app. If empty or null, all roles can use the app.

group_restrictions.description: List of group IDs (as strings) that are allowed to use the app. If empty or null, all groups can use the app.

app_installation_id.description: The ID of the app installation to update.

apps.installations.update.title: Update Zendesk App Installation

automations.update.description: Update an existing automation in Zendesk. Automations are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Use this action when you need to: - Change an automation's title, active status, or position - Modify the conditions that trigger the automation - Update the actions the automation performs - Deactivate an automation without deleting it This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The new title/name of the automation. Must be unique among all automations.

active.description: Whether the automation is active and will execute. Set to false to deactivate the automation.

actions.description: List of actions the automation will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

position.description: The position of the automation which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

conditions.description: Conditions object for automation - defines when the automation should execute.

automation_id.description: The ID of the automation to update. You can find automation IDs from the List Automations action or from the automation URL in Zendesk admin.

automations.update.title: Update Automation

custom_objects.update.description: Update an existing custom object in Zendesk. Custom objects are user-defined data structures that allow you to store and manage custom data types. Use this action when you need to: - Change a custom object's title, description, or pluralized title - Update visibility settings (include_in_list_view) - Enable or disable attachments and photos for the custom object This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: User-defined display name for the object.

description.description: User-defined description of the object.

allows_photos.description: If true, photos can be uploaded to the records of the object. If false, new photos cannot be uploaded but existing photos can still be viewed and removed.

title_pluralized.description: User-defined pluralized version of the object's title.

custom_object_key.description: The unique key identifier of the custom object. This is a path parameter that identifies which custom object to update.

allows_attachments.description: If true, file attachments can be added to the object's records. If false, new attachments can't be added to the object's records, but existing attachments on records can still be viewed and downloaded.

include_in_list_view.description: A flag setting the visibility of the object in the agent's list view. If true, all agents and admins have viewing access to the object in the Custom objects record page in the Agent Workspace. If false, only admins have viewing access.

custom_objects.update.title: Update Custom Object

custom_objects.records.update.description: Update an existing record for a custom object in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify an existing custom object record. This action updates fields on a custom object record. You can update the name, external_id, and custom_object_fields as needed.

name.description: User-defined display name for the object. If autonumbering is selected for the custom object's name field, the name isn't allowed because it's automatically generated. If uniqueness is enabled, the name must be unique.

external_id.description: An id you can use to link custom object records to external data. Set to null to remove.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car')

custom_object_fields.description: A dictionary of custom field key-value pairs. The available fields are defined in the custom object's field definitions. Keys must match field keys from the custom object definition.

custom_object_record_id.description: The ID of the custom object record to update

custom_objects.records.update.title: Update Custom Object Record

custom_statuses.update.description: Update an existing custom ticket status in Zendesk. Custom ticket statuses allow you to define additional statuses beyond the standard statuses (new, open, pending, solved, closed) for your ticket workflow. Use this action when you need to: - Change the labels shown to agents or end users for a custom status - Update the descriptions explaining when to use the status - Activate or deactivate a custom status - Modify how a custom status appears in the ticket interface This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Requires admin permissions in Zendesk.

active.description: If true, the custom status is set to active. If false, the custom status is deactivated.

agent_label.description: The dynamic content placeholder or the label displayed to agents. Maximum length is 48 characters.

description.description: The description of when the user should select this custom ticket status. Shown to agents.

end_user_label.description: The dynamic content placeholder or the label displayed to end users. Maximum length is 48 characters.

custom_status_id.description: The unique ID of the custom ticket status to update. You can find custom status IDs from the List Custom Ticket Statuses action or from the custom status URL in Zendesk admin.

end_user_description.description: The description displayed to end users. Shown to customers.

custom_statuses.update.title: Update Custom Ticket Status

deletion_schedules.update.description: Update an existing deletion schedule in Zendesk. Deletion schedules define automated rules for deleting tickets, users, attachments, or other records based on specified conditions. Use this action when you need to: - Change a deletion schedule's title, description, or active status - Modify the conditions that determine which records are deleted - Pause or reactivate a deletion schedule This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Note: The 'object' field cannot be modified after schedule creation.

title.description: The new title/name of the deletion schedule.

active.description: Whether the deletion schedule is active. Set to false to pause the schedule.

conditions.description: Conditions object for deletion schedule - defines criteria for matching records.

description.description: The description of the deletion schedule.

deletion_schedule_id.description: The unique ID of the deletion schedule to update. You can find this ID from the deletion schedule URL in Zendesk admin or from listing deletion schedules.

deletion_schedules.update.title: Update Deletion Schedule

dynamic_content.variants.update.description: Update a single variant of a dynamic content item in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify the content, locale, active status, or default status of one specific variant by its ID. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

active.description: Whether the variant is active and usable

content.description: The new content for the variant

default.description: Whether the variant is the default for the item it belongs to

locale_id.description: An active locale ID for this variant

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The ID of the dynamic content item containing the variant to update

dynamic_content_variant_id.description: The ID of the variant to update

dynamic_content.variants.update.title: Update Dynamic Content Variant

dynamic_content.variants.update_many.description: Update one or more variants of a dynamic content item in Zendesk. Use when you need to bulk update variant content, active status, or default status for a specific dynamic content item. Each variant can be identified by either its ID or locale ID. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

variants.description: List of variants to update. Each variant must include either an 'id' or 'locale_id', and can optionally include 'content', 'active', and 'default'.

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The ID of the dynamic content item whose variants you want to update

dynamic_content.variants.update_many.title: Update Many Dynamic Content Variants

macros.update.description: Update an existing macro in Zendesk. Macros are predefined responses that agents can apply to tickets to quickly perform common actions. Use this action when you need to: - Change a macro's title or description - Modify the actions the macro performs (e.g., change status, priority, or assignee) - Activate or deactivate a macro - Restrict macro access to specific users or groups This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The title of the macro.

active.description: Whether the macro should be displayed in the UI. Use false to hide the macro without deleting it.

actions.description: List of actions the macro will perform. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

macro_id.description: The ID of the macro to update. You can find macro IDs from the List Macros action or from the macro URL in Zendesk admin.

description.description: The description of the macro explaining what it does.

restriction.description: Who may access the macro. Null when everyone in the account can access it.

macros.update.title: Update Macro

automations.update_many.description: Update multiple automations in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update automation settings such as position, active status, or title for multiple automations at once. Note: You might be restricted from updating some default automations. If included in a bulk update, the unrestricted automations will be updated. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

automations.description: List of automations to update. Each automation must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position', 'active', and 'title'.

automations.update_many.title: Update Many Automations

macros.update_many.description: Update multiple macros in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update macro settings such as position or active status for multiple macros at once. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

macros.description: List of macros to update. Each macro must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position' and 'active'.

macros.update_many.title: Update Many Macros

object_triggers.update_many.description: Update multiple custom object triggers in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update trigger settings such as position, active status, or title for multiple custom object triggers at once. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

triggers.description: List of custom object triggers to update. Each trigger must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position' and 'active'.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car', 'order'). This is a path parameter that identifies which custom object's triggers to update.

object_triggers.update_many.title: Update Many Object Triggers

organizations.update_many.description: Bulk update multiple Zendesk organizations in a single request. Use when you need to update organization details such as name, notes, details, domain names, or tags for multiple organizations at once. The action is queued as a background job - use the job_status URL to poll for completion. Maximum 100 organizations per request. Note: Agents without permission restrictions can only update 'notes' on organizations.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of organization IDs to update (max 100). Required if external_ids is not provided.

external_ids.description: Comma-separated list of external organization IDs to update (max 100). Required if ids is not provided.

organizations.description: List of organizations to update. Each organization must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'name', 'notes', 'details', 'external_id', 'domain_names', and 'tags'. Agents without permission restrictions can only update 'notes'.

organizations.update_many.title: Update Many Zendesk Organizations

tickets.update_many.description: Update multiple tickets in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update ticket fields such as status, priority, tags, assignee, or group for multiple tickets at once. The API accepts up to 100 ticket objects per request. Changes are processed asynchronously and return a job_status object for tracking progress.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of ticket IDs to update. Can be used as an alternative to passing ticket objects in the body. When provided, tickets matching these IDs will be updated with the values from the ticket objects.

tickets.description: List of ticket update objects. Each object must include an 'id' field and can optionally include 'status', 'priority', 'tags', 'custom_status_id', 'assignee_id', and 'group_id'. Maximum 100 tickets per request.

tickets.update_many.title: Update Many Tickets

triggers.update_many.description: Update multiple ticket triggers in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update trigger settings such as position, active status, or category for multiple triggers at once. This action allows you to update the order (position) or activate/deactivate multiple triggers efficiently. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

triggers.description: List of triggers to update. Each trigger must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'active', 'position', and 'category_id'.

triggers.update_many.title: Update Many Ticket Triggers

users.update_many.description: Bulk update multiple Zendesk users in a single request. Use when you need to apply the same or different updates to up to 100 users at once. Provide either a single `user` object to apply identical changes to all specified users, or an array of `users` objects for individual updates per user. The operation is asynchronous and returns a job_status that you can poll to track completion. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will apply the same updates again.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of Zendesk user IDs to update (max 100). Use this when you have the numeric user IDs. Required if external_ids is not provided.

user.description: Individual user fields to update for bulk operation.

users.description: Array of user objects to update each user individually. Use this when you need to apply different updates to different users. The number of user objects should match the number of IDs provided.

external_ids.description: Comma-separated list of external user IDs to update (max 100). Use this when you have external IDs assigned to users. Required if ids is not provided.

users.update_many.title: Update Many Users

views.update_many.description: Update multiple views in Zendesk in a single request. Use when you need to bulk update view settings such as position, active status, or title for multiple views at once. Note: You might be restricted from updating some default views. If included in a bulk update, the unrestricted views will be updated. This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

views.description: List of views to update. Each view must include an 'id' and can optionally include 'position', 'active', and 'title'.

views.update_many.title: Update Many Views

object_triggers.update.description: Update an existing custom object trigger in Zendesk. Triggers define automated actions that execute when specific conditions are met on custom object records. Use this action when you need to: - Change a trigger's title or description - Enable or disable a trigger - Modify the conditions that cause the trigger to fire - Update the actions the trigger performs This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The title of the trigger. Required in the trigger object for updates.

active.description: Whether the trigger is active. Active triggers will execute when their conditions are met.

actions.description: An array of actions the trigger performs when its conditions are met. Each action defines what happens when the trigger fires.

conditions.description: An object that describes the circumstances under which the trigger performs its actions. Contains 'all' and/or 'any' arrays of condition objects with 'field', 'operator', and 'value'.

trigger_id.description: The unique identifier of the trigger to update. This is a path parameter.

description.description: A description of what the trigger does.

custom_object_key.description: The unique key identifier of the custom object that owns the trigger. This is a path parameter.

object_triggers.update.title: Update Object Trigger

organization_fields.update.description: Update a custom organization field in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify an existing organization field's properties such as title, type, description, options, or other settings. All existing custom_field_options must be included on update — omitted options will be deleted. Returns the updated organization field object.

key.description: A unique key that identifies this custom field. Must consist of only letters, numbers, and underscores. Cannot be only numbers.

tag.description: Optional tag for checkbox type fields

title.description: The title of the custom field

active.description: If true, this field is available for use. If false, the field is hidden from users.

position.description: Ordering of the field relative to other fields. Lower values appear first.

description.description: User-defined description of the field's purpose

relationship_filter.description: Filter definition for autocomplete in lookup fields.

custom_field_options.description: Required for dropdown or multiselect types. For updates: all existing options must be included (omitted options will be deleted). Pass null id for new options, include id for existing options.

organization_field_id.description: The ID of the organization field to update

regexp_for_validation.description: Regular expression pattern for validating regexp type fields

organization_fields.update.title: Update Organization Field

organizations.tags.update.description: Add organization tags in Zendesk. Use when you need to tag an organization for categorization, filtering, or automation purposes. Tags are appended to the organization's existing tags. This action is idempotent — adding the same tag multiple times will not create duplicates in the organization's tag list.

tags.description: An array of tag names to add to the organization. Tags will be appended to the existing tags list.

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization to add tags to

organizations.tags.update.title: Add Organization Tags

custom_objects.permission_policies.updat.description: Update an existing permission policy for a custom object in Zendesk. Permission policies control which records of a custom object users with a specific role can access. Use this action when you need to: - Modify record access permissions (create, read, update, delete) for a custom role - Add or remove exceptions to what records users can access - Configure group-based exclusions for custom object record permissions This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

id.description: The permission policy ID. Use 'custom-role-{custom_role_id}' for custom roles or 'end-user' for the end user system role.

records.description: Permission settings for different record operations.

custom_object_key.description: The key of the custom object

custom_objects.permission_policies.updat.title: Update Permission Policy

resource_collections.update.description: Update an existing resource collection in Zendesk. Resource collections are groups of related resources (like triggers, automations, or ticket fields) that can be managed together. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a resource collection - Modify the resources included in a collection - Update the configuration of an existing collection This action is idempotent - re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

name.description: The new name for the resource collection. Must be unique among all resource collections.

resources.description: List of resources to include in the collection. Each resource object should include 'type' (e.g., 'triggers', 'ticket_fields') and 'resource_id' or 'identifier'.

resource_collection_id.description: The ID of the resource collection to update. This is a required path parameter.

resource_collections.update.title: Update Resource Collection

side_conversations.update.description: Update a side conversation on a ticket in Zendesk. Use this action to modify the state (open/closed) or subject of an existing side conversation attached to a ticket. Use when you need to: - Close a side conversation that has been resolved - Reopen a closed side conversation - Update the subject line of a side conversation This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

state.description: The new state of the side conversation. Allowed values: 'open' or 'closed'.

subject.description: The updated subject of the side conversation.

ticket_id.description: The ticket identifier. Must be a valid ticket ID that exists in your Zendesk account.

side_conversations.update.title: Update Side Conversation

recipient_addresses.update.description: Update an existing support address in Zendesk. Support addresses are email addresses that receive customer inquiries and can be configured per brand. Use this action when you need to: - Change the name of a support address - Set or change the default support address for the account - Associate a support address with a different brand Note: You cannot change the email address of an existing support address.

name.description: The new name for the support address. This is the display name used to identify the address in Zendesk.

default.description: Whether to set this address as the account's default support address. Set to true to make it the default, false otherwise.

brand_id.description: The ID of the brand to associate with this support address. Use this to link the address to a specific brand.

support_address_id.description: The ID of the support address to update. This is a required path parameter that identifies the specific recipient address.

recipient_addresses.update.title: Update Support Address

targets.update.description: Update an existing target in Zendesk. Targets are endpoints that receive data when triggers fire (e.g., HTTP targets, email targets, webhook targets). Use this action when you need to: - Change a target's title - Activate or deactivate a target - Update target-specific properties This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

data.description: Additional target data to update. Provide any target-specific fields to modify. This allows updating target-type-specific properties beyond title and active status.

title.description: The new title of the target

active.description: Whether the target is active

target_id.description: The numeric ID of the target to update

targets.update.title: Update Zendesk Target

ticket_fields.update.description: Update an existing ticket field in Zendesk. Ticket fields define the structure and properties of custom fields on tickets. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a ticket field or update its title - Update the description or agent-only description - Change the field's position in the ticket form - Enable or disable a ticket field - Set visibility and editability for portal and agents - Make fields required for solving tickets or creating requests - Configure validation patterns for regexp fields - Set tags for checkbox fields This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result. Requires admin permissions.

tag.description: For checkbox fields only. A tag added to tickets when the checkbox field is selected

title.description: The title of the ticket field

active.description: Whether this field is available

creator.description: If true, displays the creator_user_id and creator_app_name properties in the response. If the ticket field is created by an app, creator_app_name is the name of the app and creator_user_id is -1. If the ticket field is not created by an app, then creator_app_name is null.

position.description: The relative position of the ticket field on a ticket. Note that for accounts with ticket forms, positions are controlled by the different forms

required.description: If true, agents must enter a value in the field to change the ticket status to solved

description.description: Describes the purpose of the ticket field to users

sub_type_id.description: For system ticket fields of type priority and status. Defaults to 0. A priority sub type of 1 removes the Low and Urgent options. A status sub type of 1 adds the On-Hold option

agent_can_edit.description: Whether this field is editable by agents

ticket_field_id.description: The ID of the ticket field to update

title_in_portal.description: The title of the ticket field for end users in Help Center

agent_description.description: A description of the ticket field that only agents can see

visible_in_portal.description: Whether this field is visible to end users in Help Center

editable_in_portal.description: Whether this field is editable by end users in Help Center

required_in_portal.description: If true, end users must enter a value in the field to create the request

collapsed_for_agents.description: If true, the field is shown to agents by default. If false, the field is hidden alongside infrequently used fields. Classic interface only

regexp_for_validation.description: For regexp fields only. The validation pattern for a field value to be deemed valid

ticket_fields.update.title: Update Ticket Field

tickets.tags.update.description: Update tags on a Zendesk ticket via PUT request to /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/tags. Use when you need to add, replace, or manage tags on an existing ticket. This operation replaces all existing tags with the provided list.

tags.description: An array of tag names to set on the ticket. Using this endpoint replaces all existing tags on the ticket with the provided tags.

ticket_id.description: The ID of the ticket to update tags for.

tickets.tags.update.title: Update Zendesk Ticket Tags

triggers.update.description: Update an existing ticket trigger in Zendesk. Triggers are business rules that automatically perform actions on tickets when certain conditions are met. Use this action when you need to: - Change a trigger's title, active status, position, or description - Modify the conditions that trigger the action - Update the actions the trigger performs - Reassign a trigger to a different category - Deactivate a trigger without deleting it This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The new title/name of the trigger. Must be unique among all triggers.

active.description: Whether the trigger is active and will execute.

actions.description: List of actions the trigger will perform when triggered. Each action specifies a field to modify and the value to set.

position.description: The position of the trigger which specifies the order it will be executed. Lower numbers execute first.

conditions.description: Conditions object for trigger - defines when the trigger should execute.

trigger_id.description: The ID of the trigger to update. You can find trigger IDs from the List Triggers action or from the trigger URL in Zendesk admin.

category_id.description: The ID of the category to assign the trigger to. Categories help organize triggers in the Zendesk admin interface.

description.description: A description of what the trigger does.

triggers.update.title: Update Ticket Trigger

trigger_categories.update.description: Update an existing trigger category in Zendesk. Trigger categories are used to organize ticket triggers in the Zendesk admin interface. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a trigger category - Change the display order of a trigger category - Update both name and position of a trigger category This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

name.description: The new name of the trigger category. Must be unique among all trigger categories.

position.description: The new position of the trigger category which specifies the order it will be displayed. Lower numbers appear first.

trigger_category_id.description: The ID of the ticket trigger category to update.

trigger_categories.update.title: Update Trigger Category

user_fields.update.description: Update an existing user field in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify the title, description, options, or other properties of a custom user field. Supports updating text, checkbox, dropdown, multiselect, date, integer, decimal, regexp validation, and lookup types. Only administrators can update user fields.

title.description: The new title (label) displayed for this custom field

active.description: If true, this field is available for use

position.description: Ordering of the field relative to other user fields

raw_title.description: Dynamic content placeholder for title (supports i18n placeholders)

description.description: New user-defined description of this field's purpose

user_field_id.description: The numeric ID of the user field to update. This is the field's unique numeric identifier in Zendesk, not the field key.

raw_description.description: Dynamic content placeholder for description (supports i18n placeholders)

relationship_filter.description: Filter configuration for relationship-type user fields.

custom_field_options.description: Updated options for dropdown or multiselect fields. Each option has a name (display) and value (internal tag).

regexp_for_validation.description: Regular expression pattern for validating field values

user_fields.update.title: Update Zendesk User Field

user_profiles.update_by_identifier.description: Partially updates a user profile in Zendesk by identifier. Use when you need to modify specific fields of an existing profile without replacing the entire profile. This action uses JSON merge patch semantics — only provided fields are updated. Use this action when you have an existing profile identifier and need to update specific profile attributes, identifiers, or the profile name. The identifier must follow the format source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value.

name.description: Person's name to set on the profile

source.description: Source application/system for the profile (e.g., 'company'). Cannot be 'zendesk' as it is reserved.

attributes.description: JSON schema compliant object containing profile attributes/details

identifier.description: Profile identifier in format source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value (e.g., company:contact:email:john@example.com). All identifiers must belong to a single user and profile.

identifiers.description: List of identifiers for the profile. Each identifier must have a type and value.

user_profiles.update_by_identifier.title: Update Zendesk User Profile

user_profiles.update.description: Partially updates a user profile in Zendesk by profile ID. Use when you need to modify specific fields of an existing profile without replacing the entire profile. This action uses JSON merge patch semantics — only provided fields are updated. Use this action when you have a profile ID and need to update specific profile attributes, identifiers, name, source, or type. This is different from UpdateUserProfile which uses identifier lookup instead.

name.description: Person's name to set on the profile

source.description: Source application/system for the profile (e.g., 'company'). Cannot be 'zendesk' as it is reserved.

attributes.description: JSON schema compliant object containing profile attributes/details

profile_id.description: The unique ID of the Sunshine profile to update. This is the profile ID returned when the profile was created.

identifiers.description: List of identifiers for the profile. Each identifier must have a type and value.

user_profiles.update.title: Update Zendesk User Profile By ID

users.identities.update.description: Update a user identity in Zendesk. Use when you need to modify an identity's verified status or other updatable fields. Note: the 'primary' field cannot be changed via this endpoint - use the Make Identity Primary endpoint instead.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user who owns the identity

verified.description: If true, marks the identity as verified. Deprecated - use verification_method instead for more accurate verification states.

user_identity_id.description: The numeric ID of the user identity to update

users.identities.update.title: Update User Identity

users.me.settings.update.description: Update the settings for the currently authenticated Zendesk user. Use when modifying UI preferences like keyboard shortcuts, onboarding tooltips, theme preferences, or shared views order. This action modifies the caller's own settings only.

settings.description: User settings to update. Can include lotus, admin_center, and shared_views_order.

users.me.settings.update.title: Update Current User Settings

users.profiles.update.description: Create or update a user profile for a specific Zendesk user by user ID and identifier. Use when you need to establish or modify a unified customer view for an existing Zendesk user. The profile is identified by both the user_id (path) and the identifier (query parameter). This endpoint uses PUT semantics - if a profile matching the identifier exists, it will be updated; otherwise, a new profile will be created. Use this action when you have a specific Zendesk user ID and need to create or update a profile using an identifier like email, phone number, or external ID.

profile.description: Profile object containing the profile data with name, identifiers, and optional attributes

user_id.description: The Zendesk user ID (numeric string) of the user to associate with the profile

identifier.description: Profile lookup identifier in format 'source:type:identifier_type:identifier_value' (e.g., 'company:contact:email:user@example.com'). This identifies which profile to create or update for the specified user.

users.profiles.update.title: Update Users Profiles

users.tags.update.description: Update (replace) tags for a specific Zendesk user. Use when you need to assign or modify tags on a user account for organizing, filtering, or categorizing user data. This action replaces all existing tags on the user with the provided list.

tags.description: An array of tag strings to assign to the user. This will replace all existing tags on the user with the provided list. Tags are used to categorize and organize users.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user whose tags to update. This is the user ID found in ticket payloads or user search results.

users.tags.update.title: Update User Tags

views.update.description: Update an existing view in Zendesk. Views are saved searches that allow agents to filter and organize tickets. Use this action when you need to: - Change a view's title, description, or active status - Modify a view's position in the list - Update a view's conditions or display settings - Make a view the default view This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: The title of the view

active.description: Whether the view is active

default.description: If true, the view is a default view

view_id.description: The ID of the view to update

position.description: The position of the view in the list

description.description: The description of the view

views.update.title: Update View

account.settings.update.description: Update Zendesk account-level settings including tickets, branding, localization, routing, and more. Use when you need to configure or modify account-wide settings that affect all agents and end users. Requires admin privileges to update most settings. Settings changes are persistent and affect all users.

settings.description: The account settings to update. Must include at least one setting category.

account.settings.update.title: Update Zendesk Account Settings

attachments.update.description: Updates an attachment's malware access override setting. Use when you need to enable or restrict agent access to attachments that have been flagged for malware.

attachment_id.description: The unique ID of the attachment to update

malware_access_override.description: If true, allows agents to access attachments with detected malware. If false, restricts access to malware-detected attachments.

attachments.update.title: Update Zendesk Attachment

custom_objects.fields.update.description: Update an existing custom object field in Zendesk. Custom object fields define the structure and properties of data within a custom object. Use this action when you need to: - Rename a custom object field - Update the description or display properties - Change the field's position in the UI - Enable or disable a field - Set validation patterns or make fields required This action is idempotent — re-running with the same parameters will produce the same result.

title.description: User-defined display name for the field.

active.description: If true, the field is active and can be used. If false, the field is inactive and hidden in the UI.

position.description: Position of the field in the UI. Lower values are displayed first.

required.description: If true, the field is required when creating or updating records. If false, the field is optional.

description.description: User-defined description of the field.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object (e.g., 'car'). This is a path parameter that identifies the parent custom object.

regexp_for_validation.description: A regular expression pattern used to validate the field value. Only applies to text-type fields.

custom_object_field_key_or_id.description: The key or id of a custom object field. This can be either the human-readable key (e.g., 'make') or the numeric ID of the field.

custom_objects.fields.update.title: Update Custom Object Field

dynamic_content.update.description: Update a dynamic content item in Zendesk. The only attribute that can be changed is the name. Use when you need to rename an existing dynamic content item after confirming its ID. Note: Dynamic content items are used to store multilingual content for use in triggers, automations, and macros. Updating the name affects all references to this item.

name.description: The new name for the dynamic content item. The name must be unique and is used as the identifier when referencing this item in triggers, automations, or dynamic content templates.

dynamic_content_item_id.description: The unique ID of the dynamic content item to update. You can get this ID from the item's URL or by listing dynamic content items.

dynamic_content.update.title: Update Dynamic Content Item

requests.update.description: Update a ticket request in Zendesk with a comment or collaborators. Use when you need to modify request fields like status, priority, or add comments after confirming the request ID. After updating, re-fetch via ZENDESK_GET_REQUESTS if downstream logic depends on current data.

tags.description: Tags to set on the request. Using this replaces all existing tags.

solved.description: Whether or not the request is solved. An end user can set this if 'can_be_solved_by_me' is true for that user.

comment.description: Comment object for adding a comment to the request.

group_id.description: The ID of the group to assign the request to.

request_id.description: The ID of the request to update. Find this ID from the request URL or from a list requests action.

assignee_id.description: The ID of the agent to assign the request to. The agent must be a member of the group the request is assigned to.

custom_fields.description: Custom field values to set on the request. Each item should include 'id' (field ID) and 'value'.

requests.update.title: Update Request

custom_objects.records.upsert.description: Create or update a custom object record in Zendesk by external_id or name. Use when you need to create a new record or update an existing one based on either its external_id (preferred) or name. If a record matching the external_id or name exists, it will be updated. If no matching record is found, a new one will be created. This action is idempotent and safe to retry. Note: Either external_id or name (or both) must be provided to identify the record. If both are provided, external_id takes precedence for matching.

name.description: The name of a custom object record. If a record with this name exists (and no external_id matches), it will be updated. If no record is found and external_id is provided, a new record will be created.

external_id.description: The external id of a custom object record. If a record with this external_id exists, it will be updated. If not found and name is provided, a new record will be created with this external_id.

record_data.description: Schema for a custom object record.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object. This is a user-defined unique identifier for the custom object type.

custom_objects.records.upsert.title: Upsert Custom Object Record By External ID or Name

accounts.available.description: Verify if a subdomain name is available for use in Zendesk. Returns a success boolean indicating whether the subdomain can be registered. Use when checking if a desired subdomain name is available before creating a new Zendesk account or subdomain.

check_subdomain.description: The subdomain name to verify. The name cannot contain underscores, hyphens, or spaces.

accounts.available.title: Verify Subdomain Availability

recipient_addresses.verify.description: Verify a support address forwarding in Zendesk. This action sends a verification request for the specified support address to confirm that the address is properly configured and can receive email forwarding. Use this action when you need to: - Verify a newly created support address is working correctly - Re-verify an existing support address after configuration changes - Confirm email forwarding is properly set up for a support address This action is idempotent — verifying an already-verified address will return success.

support_address_id.description: The ID of the support address to verify. You can find this ID from the support address listing or from the address details in Zendesk admin.

recipient_addresses.verify.title: Verify Support Address

users.identities.verify.description: Set a user identity as verified in Zendesk. This action marks an email address or other identity as confirmed, indicating the user has proven ownership. Use when you need to manually verify a user's identity after they have completed an out-of-band verification process or when you want to override the verification status for administrative purposes. Note: This action cannot verify the account owner's email identity due to security restrictions.

user_id.description: The numeric ID of the user

user_identity_id.description: The numeric ID of the user identity to verify

users.identities.verify.title: Verify User Identity

attachments.upload.description: Upload a file attachment to Zendesk. Returns an attachment object with an ID that can be used to attach the file to a ticket comment. Use when you need to add files (documents, images, logs, etc.) to Zendesk tickets. The upload token returned is valid for 60 minutes. After uploading, attach the file to a ticket by including the attachment token in your ticket comment. Public call is POST /api/v2/uploads?filename={filename} with the raw file bytes. filename is the name Zendesk stores; content is those bytes. Content-Type is application/octet-stream.

filename.description: File name Zendesk stores on the upload. Required filename query parameter.

content.description: Raw file bytes as a string. Sent as the POST body.

attachments.upload.title: Upload Zendesk Attachment

custom_objects.records.attachments.creat.description: Create an attachment for a custom object record in Zendesk. Use when you need to attach files (documents, images, etc.) to a custom object record. The file is uploaded as a multipart/form-data request. The response includes the attachment details and malware scan status. Public call is multipart POST /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/{record_id}/attachments with the uploaded_data file field. The handwritten handler sends that form.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object.

record_id.description: The id of a custom object record.

filename.description: File name stored on the attachment.

content.description: File bytes sent as the uploaded_data multipart field.

custom_objects.records.attachments.creat.title: Create Custom Object Record Attachment

organizations.tags.delete.description: Remove all tags from a Zendesk organization. Use when you need to clear organization tags as part of cleanup or reorganization tasks. This action is irreversible — the tags will be permanently removed from the organization and cannot be recovered once deleted. DELETE /api/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/tags. Zendesk's curl sample sends a JSON tags array; pass tags as a comma-separated list to remove those tags. Omitting tags issues the body-less DELETE.

organization_id.description: The ID of the organization whose tags will be removed.

tags.description: Comma-separated tag names to remove. Matches the JSON tags array on DELETE.

organizations.tags.delete.title: Delete Organization Tags

tickets.tags.delete.description: Remove tags from a Zendesk ticket. This action is irreversible; once tags are removed, they cannot be recovered without re-adding them. Use when you need to clean up ticket tags, remove outdated labels, or clear all tags from a ticket. DELETE /api/v2/tickets/{ticket_id}/tags. When tags is set, the handwritten handler sends the documented JSON body {"tags":[...]}.

ticket_id.description: The ID of the ticket to remove tags from.

tags.description: Comma-separated tag names to remove. If omitted, the DELETE is sent without a body.

tickets.tags.delete.title: Delete Ticket Tags

users.tags.delete.description: Remove tags from a Zendesk user. Use when you need to clean up user tags, remove outdated labels, or clear all tags from a user account. This action is irreversible — once tags are removed, they cannot be recovered without re-adding them. DELETE /api/v2/users/{user_id}/tags. When tags is set, the handwritten handler sends the documented JSON body {"tags":[...]}.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to remove tags from.

tags.description: Comma-separated tag names to remove. If omitted, the DELETE is sent without a body.

users.tags.delete.title: Delete User Tags

attachments.download.description: Download the file bytes for one Zendesk ticket attachment ID. Zendesk attachment IDs first resolve to metadata. This action then downloads the provider-issued content URL and returns the file for use by other tools. GET /api/v2/attachments/{attachment_id}, then GET the attachment content_url when that URL stays on *.zendesk.com.

attachment_id.description: The attachment ID from a Zendesk ticket comment, as a string.

data.description: Provider JSON object, response text, or base64 content envelope.

attachments.download.title: Download Attachment

custom_objects.records.attachments.downl.description: Download attachment file from a Zendesk custom object record. Use when you need to retrieve the actual file content of an attachment associated with a custom object record, such as documents, images, or other files. This action returns the raw file content and can display it inline or trigger a file download depending on the inline parameter. Note: The custom object must have attachments enabled for this action to work. GET /api/v2/custom_objects/{custom_object_key}/records/{record_id}/attachments/{id}/download. Redirects are followed only while the host stays on *.zendesk.com.

custom_object_key.description: The key of a custom object.

record_id.description: The id of a custom object record.

id.description: The id of a custom object record attachment.

inline.description: If true, Zendesk is asked to display the attachment inline.

data.description: Provider JSON object, response text, or base64 content envelope.

apps.public_key.pem.description: Retrieves the public key for a specific Zendesk app in PEM format. The PEM format is a standard base64-encoded certificate format that can be used to verify that requests from the app are legitimate. Use this action when you need to verify JWTs issued by a Zendesk app or establish trust for app-based authentication. This is a read-only operation. Note: This endpoint does not require authentication and can be accessed anonymously. GET /api/v2/apps/{app_id}/public_key.pem returns the PEM text.

app_id.description: The numeric ID of the Zendesk app whose PEM public key to retrieve.

data.description: Provider JSON object, response text, or base64 content envelope.
